newsitem.title: USA: Case sees strong outlook for farm sector.
newsitem.headline: Case sees strong outlook for farm sector.

text.p: Case Corp said Thursday the fundamental outlook for the agricultural sector remains strong while conditions in the construction equipment market vary by country and economic conditions.
Strong demand for agricultural commodities continues around the world, driven by population growth and improving diets within developing nations, the company said.

In Case's construction equipment market in North America, demand remains solid as a result of sustained, strong housing starts. In Europe, the market continues to benefit from a high level of housing construction in the U.K., which is being offset by ongoing weakness in the construction sectors in France and Germany, Case said in a news release.

In the Asia Pacific region, the expected recovery of the Australian housing market is showing further promise, but has yet to be fully realized, it said. In Latin America, economic conditions in Brazil and Mexico have improved and retail sales of construction equipment are expected to be strong year-over-year.

Earlier today, Case reported 1997 second quarter earnings rose 25 percent from the same period a year ago to $137 million. Net income per share increased 24 percent to $1.82. Revenues increased nine percent to a record $1.6 billion.
Each of Case's four geographic regions contributed to the sales increase, with particularly strong year-over-year gains in the company's international markets.

"Recent acquisitions and solid retail demand supported sales growth in the quarter, particularly in higher margin equipment," said Jean-Pierre Rosso, chairman, president and chief executive officer, in a news release. "We also benefited from additional cost reduction actions that will contribute to future earnings," he added.

Consistent with 1996, Case said it continues to expect that 1997 unit production and wholesale sales will be at or below retail demand as part of the company's continuing supply chain management initiative to further reduce field inventories.
Shares of Case were trading off 15/16 to 65.
